title: Mapping Written Words to Spoken Words in a Different Language Using Only Visual Grounding
abstract: arXiv:2608.26925v1 Announce Type: new  Abstract: In many low-resource settings, even just eliciting speech for data collection is difficult. One promising approach has been to ask speakers to describe images. But how do we build models from such visually grounded speech data? Given a dataset of images with Hindi spoken captions, we consider how we can map a written English keyword to spoken realisations of that word in Hindi. Previous work trained end-to-end multimodal neural models. Instead, we explore a simpler alignment-based approach built on self-supervised speech representations. Written English tags are automatically obtained from images using off-the-shelf image captioning systems. Hindi utterances associated with the same keyword are then aligned (using self-supervised features), and alignment evidence is aggregated to identify recurring speech segments corresponding to the target word. translated_title: 仅通过视觉接地将书面文字映射到另一种语言的口语表达
translated_abstract: arXiv:2608.26925v1 公告类型：新 摘要：在许多资源匮乏的环境中，即使仅仅收集语音数据也非常困难。一种有前景的方法是要求说话者描述图像。但如何从这种视觉接地的语音数据中构建模型呢？给定一个包含印地语口语字幕的图像数据集，我们考虑如何将书面英文关键词映射到该词在印地语中的口语实现形式。先前的工作训练了端到端的多模态神经模型。相反，我们探索了一种基于自监督语音表征的更简单的对齐方法。使用现成的图像字幕系统从图像中自动获取书面英文标签。然后，将与同一关键词关联的印地语话语（使用自监督特征）进行对齐，并聚合对齐证据以识别对应目标词的重复出现的语音片段。评估关键词检测和定位的实验表明，我们的基于对齐的方法在性能上具有竞争力。
tldr: 本文提出一种基于自监督语音表征和对齐的简单方法，利用视觉接地数据将书面英文关键词映射到印地语口语表达，无需端到端神经模型，在关键词检测和定位上表现良好。
en_tdlr: This paper proposes a simple alignment-based approach using self-supervised speech representations to map written English keywords to spoken Hindi realizations from visually grounded data, achieving competitive performance in keyword spotting and localization without end-to-end neural models.
